blocks.en: French has only **two genders**: masculine (*le*) and feminine (*la*). There is no neuter. The gender is often different from Czech, so learn every word **together with its article**: not *table*, but *la table*.
There are exceptions (*la plage, la page, l'eau* are feminine, *le musée* is masculine), but these rules hold for most words.
With people the feminine often adds *-e*: *un ami → une amie, un étudiant → une étudiante*. Some words change more: *un acteur → une actrice, un chanteur → une chanteuse, un Italien → une Italienne*.

items.en: the problem (masculine, even though it ends in -e)

articles.title: Gender from the ending of a noun

blocks.en: There are no rules without exceptions, but the **ending of a noun** gives you the gender in about 80% of cases. Learn the endings in the table and **always learn the article with a new noun**.

le lycée, le musée, le trophée
la chaleur, la couleur, la peur, la fleur, la valeur

le livre, le gîte, le groupe, le disque, le musée

blocks.en: **Masculine**: days, months, seasons, languages, colours, metals, trees (*le chêne*), the cardinal points, many countries not ending in -e (*le Canada*). **Feminine**: most countries and rivers ending in **-e** (*la France, la Seine*), many sciences (*la physique*).

items.fr: Le lundi, le français, le rouge, l'été.
items.en: Monday, French, red, summer: all masculine.

items.fr: La France, la Loire, la chimie.
Un bateau, une voiture, un fromage, une boulangerie.

blocks.en: Czech gender is a bad guide: *le soleil* (masc.) is neuter in Czech, *la lune* (fem.) is masculine in Czech. Learn each noun with its article.

items.fr: La télévision est dans le salon.
items.en: The television is in the living room.

articles.title: Same word, two genders, two meanings
articles.fr: le genre qui change le sens

blocks.en: A group of French nouns changes **meaning with the gender**. Watch the article: *un tour* (a trip) and *une tour* (a tower) are different words with the same spelling.

head: masculine
feminine
rows: le poste = the post, job, set

blocks.en: Some nouns are the **same for both sexes** and only the article changes: *un / une élève, un / une collègue, un / une touriste, un / une enfant*. Others change the ending: *un étudiant / une étudiante*.

items.fr: Mon collègue s'appelle Paul, ma collègue s'appelle Anna.
items.en: My (male) colleague is called Paul, my (female) colleague Anna.

items.fr: Un enfant et une enfant sont là.
items.en: A boy and a girl are here.
My teacher is a woman. (professeur stays masculine in writing)

items.note: *Le tour* is a trip or a turn.

items.fr: La tour Eiffel est très haute.
items.en: The Eiffel Tower is very tall.

items.fr: Je fais le tour du lac.

items.en: Are you going to the post office?

checks.en: I'm going to the post office.

checks.fr: Nous faisons ___ tour de la ville.

blocks.en: Most words take *-s* in the plural, and it is **not pronounced**. You tell it is plural mainly from the article: *le livre* × *les livres*.

head: rule
singular
plural
rows: un bus, une voix, un nez
des bus, des voix, des nez

blocks.en: Before a vowel the *-s* of the article is pronounced as [z]: *les‿amis, des‿enfants*.

items.fr: Il y a des animaux au zoo.
items.en: There are animals at the zoo.

items.fr: Les journaux sont sur la table.
items.en: The newspapers are on the table.

articles.title: Special plurals: -al, -eau, -ou, les gens, les cheveux

blocks.en: Most plurals just add **-s**. These are the exceptions you need. **-al → -aux**, **-eau, -eu → -x**, a few **-ou → -x**, nouns already ending in **-s, -x, -z** stay the same.

head: singular
plural
rule
rows: 7 nouns in -ou take -x: bijou, caillou, chou, genou, hibou, joujou, pou

blocks.en: A few nouns in **-al** take **-s**: **des bals, des carnavals, des festivals, des récitals**. A few nouns in **-eau** with **-s**: **des landaus**. And **-ail → -aux**: *un travail → des travaux*, *un vitrail → des vitraux*.

items.fr: Il y a trois festivals cet été.
items.en: There are three festivals this summer.
These pieces of jewellery are expensive.

blocks.en: **Surnames do not take -s**: *les Dupont, les Martin*. **Compound nouns** follow their own rules (*des grands-mères, des porte-clés*). When in doubt use the dictionary.

items.fr: Les chevaux courent dans le pré.
items.en: The horses are running in the field.

items.fr: J'ai lu deux journaux ce matin.
items.en: I read two newspapers this morning.

checks.fr: Il y a trois ___ en ville.
checks.en: There are three festivals in town.

articles.title: Definite article: le, la, l', les

blocks.en: Czech has no articles, French puts one before almost every noun. The definite article means "the": something **known, unique or general**.

head: when
example
English
rows: a day of the week, regularly

blocks.en: Before a vowel and a silent *h*, both *le* and *la* shorten to *l'*: *l'ami, l'école, l'hôtel*.

items.note: After *aimer, adorer, détester, préférer* there is always a definite article.

items.fr: Le samedi, je joue au basket.

articles.title: More uses of le, la, les

blocks.en: The definite article is used where Czech and English have **no article**. The main cases: **general statements**, **likes and dislikes**, **days (habit)**, **body parts**, **languages and school subjects**, **prices per unit**, and **countries**.

head: use
example
English
rows: J'aime le café. Les chats sont mignons.
I like coffee. Cats are cute.
Je me lave les mains. J'ai mal à la tête.
I wash my hands. I have a headache.
Ça coûte trois euros le kilo.
It costs three euros a kilo.
La France, le Canada, les États-Unis.
Le docteur Martin, la reine Élisabeth.

blocks.en: After *aimer, adorer, détester, préférer* and for any general statement, use **le, la, les**, not *du / de la*. Compare: *J'aime le café* (in general) / *Je bois du café* (some).

sections.title: Habit with a day, and body parts

blocks.en: **Le lundi** = every Monday; **lundi** (no article) = this coming or last Monday. For the body use the article and **not the possessive** when the owner is clear from the verb: *Il lève la main, elle se brosse les dents.*

items.en: On Monday I have an exam.
The price is 5 euros a kilo.

items.fr: Les tomates coûtent deux euros le kilo.
items.en: Tomatoes cost two euros a kilo.

checks.en: It costs three euros a kilo.
a: Ça coûte trois euros le kilo.

blocks.en: The indefinite article means "a, an, one". Use it when you mention something **for the first time** or when it is **one of many**.
*Des* is the plural of *un, une*. English often leaves it out ("I have friends in Paris"), but French cannot.

items.en: I have a dog. The dog is called Max.
items.note: First *un*, then the dog is known: *le*.

items.fr: Il y a un chat dans le jardin.
items.en: There is a cat in the garden.

checks.fr: Il y a ___ livres sur la table.
checks.en: There are books on the table.
I have a dog and a cat.
a: J'ai un chien et un chat.

articles.title: Des or de? The article before an adjective

blocks.en: The plural of **un / une** is **des**. But when a **plural adjective stands before the noun** (*beau, bon, grand, petit, jeune, vieux, autre...*), **des becomes de** (or **d'** before a vowel): *de beaux livres, d'autres idées*. After the noun, nothing changes: *des livres intéressants*.

items.note: The adjective comes after, so *des* stays.

blocks.en: It is a case of **simplification**: *de + adjective + noun* behaves like *de* after a quantity word. In everyday speech many people still say *des beaux livres*, but in careful French you write *de beaux livres*.
When the adjective is part of a **fixed compound noun**, *des* stays: *des jeunes gens, des petits pois, des petits-enfants, des grands-parents, des petits déjeuners*.
After a negation *des* becomes *de* anyway (*Je n'ai pas d'amis*), so the adjective makes no difference: *Je n'ai pas de bons amis.*

items.fr: Nous avons eu de bonnes notes.

checks.task_en: Put the adjective before the noun

articles.title: Partitive article: du, de la, de l'

blocks.en: The partitive article goes before things you do **not count** but **measure**: some bread, some water. English often leaves it out or says "some".
After *aimer, adorer, détester, préférer* it is *le, la, les*. After *manger, boire, acheter, vouloir, il y a* it is usually *du, de la, des*.
The partitive article is also used with abstract things and activities: *faire du sport, jouer de la batterie, avoir de la chance* (to be lucky), *il y a du vent* (it's windy).

items.fr: Je bois du lait le matin.
items.en: I drink milk in the morning.

items.fr: On mange de la soupe ce soir.

blocks.en: In the negative *un, une, du, de la, de l', des* become **de** (*d'* before a vowel).

items.en: I have a dog. → I don't have a dog.
items.fr: J'ai un chien. → Je n'ai pas [[de]] chien.

items.en: I drink milk. → I don't drink milk.
items.fr: Je bois du lait. → Je ne bois pas [[de]] lait.

items.en: I have friends. → I don't have friends.
items.fr: J'ai des amis. → Je n'ai pas [[d']]amis.

blocks.en: *Le, la, les* stay: *J'aime le café → Je n'aime pas le café.* And after *être* nothing changes: *C'est un chien → Ce n'est pas un chien.*

head: positive
negative
rows: Il n'y a pas de pain.

blocks.en: This also applies to *jamais* and *plus*: *Je ne mange jamais de viande. Il n'y a plus de lait.*

items.fr: Il n'y a pas d'école demain.
Nous ne mangeons pas de viande.
Il n'y a plus de pain.

a: Il n'y a pas de lait.

articles.title: Contracted articles: au, aux, du, des

blocks.en: The prepositions *à* and *de* **merge** with the articles *le* and *les* into one word. With *la* and *l'* they stay separate.

items.en: I'm going to the swimming pool.

items.fr: La porte de la maison est ouverte.
items.en: The door of the house is open.

blocks.en: *Des* can be two different words: the indefinite article (*des amis* = friends) or *de + les* (*le chien des voisins* = the neighbours' dog).

checks.en: I'm going to the swimming pool.

articles.title: Quantities: beaucoup de, un kilo de

blocks.en: After expressions of quantity only **de** (*d'*) stands, without an article: *beaucoup de pain*, not *beaucoup du pain*.

items.en: I have a lot of homework.

blocks.en: Exception: *la plupart des* (most) keeps the article: *la plupart des élèves*.

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de monde.
items.en: There are a lot of people.

items.fr: Je voudrais un kilo de tomates.
items.en: I'd like a kilo of tomatoes.
How many cousins do you have?

checks.en: I have a lot of friends.
I'd like a bottle of milk.

a: Je n'ai pas beaucoup de temps.

checks.en: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
a: Tu as combien de frères et sœurs ?
Combien de frères et sœurs as-tu ?
Combien de frères et sœurs est-ce que tu as ?

example
English

He is a doctor. She is French.
en France, en bus, en bois
in France, by bus, made of wood
to be hungry, to be afraid
after de when it says the kind
un livre de cuisine, un match de foot

items.note: With an adjective an article is needed again: *C'est un bon ingénieur.*

blocks.en: When *de* links two nouns and the second says the **kind**, there is no article: *un prof de français* (a French teacher), *une salle de bains* (a bathroom), *un jeu de société* (a board game).

items.fr: Je vais au collège en bus.
items.en: I go to school by bus.

items.fr: Un café sans sucre, s'il vous plaît.

a: Un thé sans sucre, s'il vous plaît.
Un thé sans sucre, s'il te plaît.

blocks.en: Six questions that lead you to the right article. Go from the top and stop at the first one you answer yes to.

items.label: Is there a negation (*ne... pas, jamais, plus*) and not *être*?
Does an expression of quantity (*beaucoup, un kilo, combien*) stand before the word?
Are you talking about a thing in general, or about what you like?
Is the thing known, specific, unique?
items.en: → *le, la, les*: *Le chien du voisin aboie.*

items.label: Is it some amount of something uncountable?
items.en: → *du, de la, de l'*: *Je mange du pain.*

items.fr: Je ne mange pas de chocolat.
Il y a beaucoup de chocolat.
items.en: There is a lot of chocolate.

items.note: What decides is the verb the word belongs to: here *manger* (some apples), not *aimer*.
